text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait Real Estate Bank profits reach 6.2 million dinars ($20.5 million) in 1996 from 406,000 dinars in 1974, senior bank sources say.
- Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah telephones opposition MP Abdullah al-Naibari in Boston where he is conducting medical tests after a failed assassination bid earlier this month.
- Kuwaiti businessmen are the second largest investors in Egypt.

- Parliament says government plans to restore ties with countries which supported Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait should be conditional. The controversial issued was discussed in a closed parliamentary session on Saturday.
- Relations with Jordan and Yemen will resume soon, government source said. The two fellow Arab states were seen as Iraq sympathisers during the Gulf crisis.

- Kuwait stresses the need for a new United Nations Security Council resolution to oblige former occupier Iraq to implement all previous resolutions. The Security Council on Saturday unanimously warned Iraq it faced further sanctions if it did not allow U.N. arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.
- The official Kuwait News Agancy (KUNA) launches a training course for new Kuwaiti journalists.

- Revive economic boycott of Israel, senior official at the Israel Boycott Office in Kuwait says. Kuwait and the other Gulf Arab states do not have diplomatic ties with Israel and have not lifted the direct Arab economic boycott of the Jewish state.
